ops.current: modifying 看護婦. The topic あの看護婦 is marked by は

The topic あの看護婦 is marked by は, the adverb とても ('very') intensifies, and 親切 is a な-adjective (形状詞) that here appears in predicate form with the casual copula だ. Since 親切 is a な-adjective, it needs だ/です to predicate (unlike い-adjectives).
ops.issue: The explanation twice refers to 看護婦 (older gendered term), but the sentence uses 看護師. Citing a word that is not in the sentence will confuse learners.

ops.current: modificando 看護婦. O tópico あの看護婦 é marcado por は

O tópico あの看護婦 é marcado por は, o advérbio とても ('muito') intensifica, e 親切 é um adjetivo-な (形状詞) que aqui aparece em forma de predicado com a cópula casual だ. Como 親切 é adjetivo-な, ele precisa de だ/です para predicar (diferente dos adjetivos-い).

ops.full_before: の links 次 to 特急, forming 次の特急 ("the next express"), which is the topic marked by は. 何時 (read いつ here, "when"; also used as なんじ "what time") is the interrogative predicate with です. The particle か at the end turns the sentence into a question. The vocabulary focus is 特急.

ops.current: The target here is the verb 締める ('to tighten/adjust') applied to a tie

ops.full_before: The sentence chains two actions with the te-form (締めて = te-form of 締める). This form links 'to tighten the tie' to 'to go out', indicating sequence: first tighten the tie, then go out. The target here is the verb 締める ('to tighten/adjust') applied to a tie, and を marks the tie as the direct object.
ops.issue: The explanation teaches the wrong contextual sense of the target verb: 締める with ネクタイ means 'to put on/knot (a tie)', not 'to tighten/adjust'. Also affects the earlier phrase "links 'to tighten the tie' to 'to go out'".

ops.current: join ても/ては and close with ならない ('does not become acceptable')
ops.fix: join ては and close with ならない ('does not become acceptable')
ops.full_before: The target is 〜なくてはならない, which expresses obligation ('have to do'). You take the verb in the negative form without the 〜い (飲ま + ない becomes 飲まなく), join ても/ては and close with ならない ('does not become acceptable'). Literally it is something like 'if I don't drink, things won't be right', that is, 'I have to drink'. 毎日 ('every day') is just a time adverb at the start.
ops.issue: Explanation of the target grammar says to 'join ても/ては' before ならない. ても is wrong here: なくても pairs with いい/かまわない (permission), and なくてもならない is ungrammatical. Only ては belongs in なくてはならない. Teaches a false variant of the obligation pattern.

ops.current: junta-se ても/ては e fecha-se com ならない ('não se torna aceitável')
ops.fix: junta-se ては e fecha-se com ならない ('não se torna aceitável')
ops.full_before: O alvo é 〜なくてはならない, que expressa obrigação ('ter que fazer'). Pega-se o verbo na forma negativa sem o 〜い (飲ま + ない vira 飲まなく), junta-se ても/ては e fecha-se com ならない ('não se torna aceitável'). Literalmente é algo como 'se eu não tomar, a coisa não fica certa', ou seja, 'tenho que tomar'. 毎日 ('todo dia') é só um advérbio de tempo no começo.
ops.issue: Same defect as expl_en: 'junta-se ても/ては' offers ても as an alternative in なくてはならない. なくてもならない is ungrammatical (なくても goes with いい). Only ては is correct in this obligation pattern.

ops.current: the generic counter 〜つ, which counts shapeless things (here, 五つ = いつつ)
ops.fix: the generic counter 〜つ, used for things with no specific counter (here, 五つ = いつつ)
ops.full_before: The order is [object] を [quantity] [verb]. りんご ('apple') is the direct object, marked by を. 五つ ('five units') is the quantity using the generic counter 〜つ, which counts shapeless things (here, 五つ = いつつ). In Japanese, the number-counter usually comes right before the verb, not together with the noun. The verb is in 買った, the casual past form of 買う ('to buy'). The vocabulary focus is the counter 〜つ (one, two,... units).
ops.issue: 〜つ is the general-purpose counter for things lacking a dedicated counter; 'counts shapeless things' is false as stated (apples have a definite shape) and misleads learners about when to use it.

ops.current: o contador genérico 〜つ, que conta coisas sem forma específica (aqui, 五つ = いつつ)

ops.full_before: A ordem é [objeto] を [quantidade] [verbo]. りんご ('maçã') é o objeto direto, marcado por を. 五つ ('cinco unidades') é a quantidade usando o contador genérico 〜つ, que conta coisas sem forma específica (aqui, 五つ = いつつ). Em japonês, o número-contador costuma vir logo antes do verbo, não junto do substantivo. O verbo está em 買った, a forma passada casual de 買う ('comprar'). O foco de vocabulário é o contador 〜つ (um, dois,... unidades).
ops.issue: Same as expl_en: 'conta coisas sem forma específica' wrongly claims 〜つ counts shapeless things; it is the generic counter for things without a dedicated counter (a maçã tem forma definida).

ops.current: に marks 公園 (park) as the place where the action occurs.

ops.full_before: に marks 公園 (park) as the place where the action occurs. The expression たくさんの (much/many) links to the noun 桜 (cherry tree) via the particle の, forming 'many cherry trees'. を marks that set as the object, and the target 植える (to plant) appears in the plain past form 植えた. With no explicit subject, natural English uses 'they planted'.
ops.issue: Describes に as marking 'the place where the action occurs' — that is で's function. With placement verbs like 植える, に marks the destination/resulting location of the object. This blurs the fundamental に/で distinction.

Sem sujeito explícito, o português natural usa 'plantaram'.

ops.current: Quanto à(s) foto(s), é permitido (eu) ver(humilde) também?
ops.fix: A(s) foto(s) (obj.), mesmo que (eu) veja (humilde), está bem?
ops.issue: Same mis-mirror in pt: 'Quanto à(s)' trata を como tópico e 'também' lê o も concessivo como aditivo.

ops.current: でんしゃがとまったきごうそれでおくれた
ops.fix: でんしゃがとまった　それでおくれた
ops.issue: Tokenizer placeholder reading きごう ('kigou' = symbol) for the full-width space leaked into the phonetic transcription; きごう is not pronounced.

ops.current: denshagatomattakigousoredeokureta
ops.fix: denshagatomatta soredeokureta
ops.issue: Same leak in romaji: 'kigou' is an invented syllable string from the space-token placeholder, not punctuation left in (so not covered by the known issue).

ops.current: clock
ops.fix: watch
ops.issue: 時計 glossed 'clock', but in this sentence (Swiss-made, translated 'This watch') the contextual sense is 'watch'; pt gloss 'relógio' covers both, the en gloss does not.

ops.current: おかあさんにきごうおかしをきごうもらいました
ops.fix: おかあさんにおかしをもらいました
ops.issue: Kana transcription contains きごう ('kigou', the reading of 記号 'symbol') twice — the tokenizer read the two spaces in the jp as the word 記号. Extra syllables make the phonetic reading wrong.

ops.current: okaasannikigouokashiokigoumoraimashita
ops.fix: okaasanniokashiomoraimashita
ops.issue: Romaji inherits the same defect: 'kigou' inserted twice for the space characters. This is not the known punctuation/katakana issue — it adds nonexistent syllables.

ops.current: きごう
ops.fix: null (remove the space token or blank its reading)
ops.issue: Token with surface ' ' (a space) is assigned reading きごう. A whitespace token has no reading; it should be removed or have r null.

ops.current: きごう
ops.fix: null (remove the space token or blank its reading)
ops.issue: Second space-surface token also assigned reading きごう. Same defect as tokens[4].

ops.current: As for the sky, when it clouds over, it becomes cold.
ops.fix: The sky (subject) — when it clouds over, it becomes cold.
ops.issue: Literal mirror renders subject-marker が as the topic device 'As for the sky', which the corpus reserves for は. It contradicts expl_en, which correctly says が marks the subject.

ops.current: Quanto ao céu, se/quando fica nublado, fica frio (torna-se frio).
ops.fix: O céu (sujeito), quando fica nublado, fica frio (torna-se frio).
ops.issue: Same mirroring error in pt: 'Quanto ao céu' presents が as se fosse o tópico は; the corpus uses 'Quanto a...' only for は, and expl_pt correctly calls 空が sujeito.

ops.current: warm, lukewarm
ops.fix: warm
ops.issue: あたたかい glossed 'warm, lukewarm'. 'Lukewarm' (tepid, negatively not-hot) is ぬるい, not あたたかい, which means pleasantly warm; the pt gloss 'quente (agradável)' has it right.

ops.current: presentation
ops.fix: introduction (of a person)
ops.issue: 紹介 glossed as 'presentation' — a false friend from pt 'apresentação'. In English 紹介 (introducing a person) is 'introduction', never 'presentation'.

ops.current: (polite verbal copula)
ops.fix: (politeness auxiliary)
ops.issue: ます glossed as '(polite verbal copula)'. ます is a politeness auxiliary (助動詞), not a copula; calling it a copula teaches a false category (the same batch correctly labels です as copula).

ops.current: (cópula polida verbal)
ops.fix: (auxiliar de polidez)
ops.issue: Same defect in pt: ます rotulado como 'cópula polida verbal'; não é cópula, é auxiliar de polidez (the role field itself says 'auxiliar de polidez').

ops.current: Como os sapatos são sujos, (eu) lavo.
ops.fix: Como os sapatos estão sujos, (eu) lavo.
ops.issue: 'são sujos' states an inherent quality; the sentence describes a current state (shoes are dirty now, hence washing). BR-PT requires 'estão sujos' — the natural pt translation already uses it.

ops.current: おそぼさんわやさしいひとだ
ops.fix: おばあさんわやさしいひとだ
ops.issue: お祖母さん is read おばあさん, never おそぼさん. そぼ is the humble reading of 祖母 used only without the お…さん honorific frame; おそぼさん is not a Japanese word.

ops.current: osobosanwayasashiihitoda
ops.fix: obaasanwayasashiihitoda
ops.issue: Follows the wrong kana reading: 'osobosan' should be 'obaasan' (お祖母さん = おばあさん).

ops.current: そぼ
ops.fix: ばあ
ops.issue: Token 祖母 inside お祖母さん is read ばあ (おばあさん), not そぼ; そぼ only occurs in the bare humble form 祖母 without お…さん.

ops.current: This noun compound is the predicate, closed by the copula だ.
ops.fix: This noun phrase is the predicate, closed by the copula だ.
ops.full_before: The structure is 'topic は + [adjective + noun] + だ'. The i-adjective やさしい ('kind') comes before the noun 人 ('person') to qualify it: やさしい人 ('kind person'). This noun compound is the predicate, closed by the copula だ. お祖母さん uses the prefix お and the suffix さん, making 'grandmother' polite and affectionate.
ops.issue: やさしい人 (adjective + noun) is a noun phrase, not a 'noun compound'; the terminology is incorrect in a grammar explanation.

ops.current: Esse substantivo composto é o predicado, fechado pela cópula だ.
ops.fix: Esse sintagma nominal é o predicado, fechado pela cópula だ.
ops.full_before: A estrutura é 'tópico は + [adjetivo + substantivo] + だ'. O い-adjetivo やさしい ('gentil') vem antes do substantivo 人 ('pessoa') para qualificá-lo: やさしい人 ('pessoa gentil'). Esse substantivo composto é o predicado, fechado pela cópula だ. お祖母さん usa o prefixo お e o sufixo さん, deixando 'avó' cortês e afetivo.
ops.issue: やさしい人 is a sintagma nominal (adjetivo + substantivo), not a 'substantivo composto'; the terminology is incorrect and inconsistent with the token role, which correctly says 'núcleo do sintagma nominal'.

ops.current: まどをあけましたきごうするとかぜがはいってきました
ops.fix: まどをあけましたするとかぜがはいってきました
ops.issue: Stray reading きごう ('symbol') inserted into the kana where the inter-sentence space is — a tokenizer artifact (the whitespace token was given the reading きごう). The sentence contains no such word.

ops.current: madooakemashitakigousurutokazegahaittekimashita
ops.fix: madooakemashitasurutokazegahaittekimashita
ops.issue: Same artifact as kana: 'kigou' (the word for 'symbol') inserted between the two clauses; it is not part of the sentence.

ops.current: きごう
ops.fix: null (whitespace separator has no reading)
ops.issue: The whitespace separator token (s: " ") was assigned the reading きごう ('symbol'), a tokenizer artifact. A space has no reading; it should be null like other silent tokens.

ops.current: しゅみでえをえがいている
ops.fix: しゅみでえをかいている
ops.issue: In the collocation 絵を描く, 描く is standardly read かく (えをかく); えがく is used for figurative/abstract objects (夢・情景を描く) and えをえがく sounds redundant and unnatural to natives. Teaching えがい here misleads learners.

ops.current: shumideeoegaiteiru
ops.fix: shumideeokaiteiru
ops.issue: Follows the nonstandard reading: 'egaiteiru' should be 'kaiteiru' for 絵を描いている.

ops.current: えがい
ops.fix: かい
ops.issue: Token 描い in 絵を描いている should be read かい (from かく), not えがい; えがく does not naturally take 絵 as its direct object.

ops.current: fechado por でした, a forma polida e passada do copula です
ops.fix: fechado por でした, a forma polida e passada da cópula です
ops.full_before: A frase tem advérbio + tópico + predicado nominal. やはり exprime "como eu esperava / no fim das contas", confirmando uma previsão. 今日は marca "hoje" como tópico com は (sobre o qual se comenta). 雨 (chuva) é o predicado nominal, fechado por でした, a forma polida e passada do copula です, ou seja, "era/foi chuva".
ops.issue: Wrong gender and missing accent in Portuguese: 'cópula' is feminine, so 'do copula' should be 'da cópula'.

ops.current: much, a lot
ops.fix: very
ops.issue: とても here intensifies the adjective 古い, meaning 'very'; the gloss 'much, a lot' fits a quantity sense that does not apply in this sentence (the same corpus glosses とても as 'very' elsewhere).

ops.current: At the party, there are many people wearing kimonos.
ops.fix: At the festival, people who wear kimono are many.
ops.issue: 祭り means (traditional) festival, not 'party' (that would be パーティー). The main en translation correctly says 'festivals'; the literal contradicts it and teaches a wrong sense.

ops.current: わたしのかぞくわよんにんだ
ops.fix: わたしのかぞくわよにんだ
ops.issue: 四人 (four people) is read よにん, an irregular reading; よんにん is incorrect. The kana transcription teaches a wrong pronunciation.

ops.current: よん
ops.fix: よ
ops.issue: In the counter compound 四人 the numeral 四 is read よ (yo-nin), not よん. Token reading propagates the wrong pronunciation.

ops.current: watashinokazokuwayonninda
ops.fix: watashinokazokuwayoninda
ops.issue: Romaji inherits the wrong reading of 四人: should be yonin (よにん), not yonnin.

ops.current: As for the night, I take a bath.
ops.fix: At night (に), (I) enter the bath.
ops.issue: 'As for the night' wrongly mirrors 夜に as a topic (は) construction; に here marks time, and there is no topic particle. lit_pt correctly renders it as 'À noite (に)'; lit_en should match.

ops.current: to think, to feel
ops.fix: to think, to consider
ops.issue: 'to feel' is not a sense of 考える (to think, to consider); in this sentence 考えられている means 'is thought/believed'. The pt gloss 'pensar, achar' is correct; the en gloss should not include 'feel'.

ops.current: pa-tei-detabetarinondarishimashita
ops.fix: pa-ti-detabetarinondarishimashita
ops.issue: The small-kana combination てぃ (ティ) is romanized 'tei' instead of 'ti': パーティー = paatii. This is a wrong syllable, distinct from the already-known punctuation/unromanized-katakana issues.

ops.current: As for the police station (the place where), there are two policemen.
ops.fix: At the police station (the place where), there are two policemen.
ops.issue: Same defect as lit_pt: 'As for...' implies topic-は, but 交番に is a locative に phrase. The literal mirror misrepresents the particle's function.

ops.current: Quanto à delegacia (lugar onde), policiais existem (em número de) dois.
ops.fix: Na delegacia (lugar onde), policiais existem (em número de) dois.
ops.issue: The 'Quanto a...' device is the corpus mirror for は, but here the phrase is 交番に (locative に, no は). Rendering に as 'Quanto à' teaches a false particle mapping; elsewhere in the corpus に/で/まで phrases use prepositions (cf. 'No mar', 'Até a estação').

ops.current: わたしわきごうまいあさきごうぱんをきごうたべる
ops.fix: わたしわまいあさぱんをたべる
ops.issue: The spaces in the spaced jp sentence were transcribed as きごう ('symbol') three times, inserting nonexistent syllables into the phonetic reading (wa-ta-shi-wa-KI-GO-U-ma-i-a-sa...).

ops.current: watashiwakigoumaiasakigoupanokigoutaberu
ops.fix: watashiwamaiasapanotaberu
ops.issue: Same space-token artifact as kana: 'kigou' inserted three times into the romanization. This is beyond the known punctuation/katakana romaji issue — it adds phantom syllables.

ops.current: this / that
ops.fix: this
ops.issue: この is strictly proximal ('this'); glossing it as 'this / that' conflates it with その/あの. The pt gloss ('este / esta') is correct, so the two glosses also disagree.

ops.current: Quanto à África, muito é ampla.
ops.fix: Quanto à África, é muito ampla.
ops.issue: Adverb misplaced: 'muito é ampla' is ungrammatical Portuguese (reads as 'much is ample'). Even a literal mirror must be parseable pt; lit_en correctly has 'it's very vast'.

ops.current: いちにちにおきゅうりょうがはいる
ops.fix: ついたちにおきゅうりょうがはいる
ops.issue: １日 meaning 'the 1st of the month' (as en/pt/expl all state) is read ついたち, not いちにち. いちにち means 'one day/all day' and contradicts the taught meaning. Romaji 'ichinichini' has the same error (should be tsuitachini).

ops.current: いち
ops.fix: ついたち (fuse １+日 into one token)
ops.issue: Token readings １=いち and 日=にち are wrong for 'the 1st (of the month)'; １日 is the fused reading ついたち. The two tokens should be merged (or re-split) so the reading is ついたち, not いち+にち.

ops.current: dia(do mês)
ops.fix: dia (do mês)
ops.issue: Missing space in the pt gloss: 'dia(do mês)' should be 'dia (do mês)'.

ops.current: I felt sad after breaking up with her.
ops.fix: I'm sad that I broke up with her.
ops.issue: 悲しい is non-past: the speaker is sad NOW because of the breakup (expl itself says the te-form is causal). 'I felt sad after...' shifts the sadness to the past and reads as mere sequence; lit_en correctly has 'I'm sad'.

ops.current: big, tall
ops.fix: big; (here) loud
ops.issue: Gloss 'big, tall' fits another sense of 大きい (physical size/stature); in 大きな声 the contextual meaning is 'loud (voice)'. 'tall' is plainly wrong here. (pt gloss 'alto' is fine since 'voz alta' = loud voice.)

ops.current: Quanto a avo (tema), todo ano, verduras (objeto) planta (presente polido).
ops.fix: Quanto à avó (tema), todo ano, verduras (objeto) planta (presente polido).
ops.issue: Accent typo: 'avo' should be 'avó' (grandmother); also needs crase with the feminine noun ('Quanto à avó').

ops.current: きょうわなんもかいませんでした
ops.fix: きょうわなにもかいませんでした
ops.issue: 何も in this polite sentence (買いませんでした) reads なにも; なんも is a casual/colloquial contraction that clashes with the register and is not the form a course should teach. Romaji 'nanmo' has the same error (should be nanimo).

ops.current: なん
ops.fix: なに
ops.issue: Reading of 何 in 何も should be なに (standard なにも), not なん; なんも is colloquial and inconsistent with the polite sentence being taught.

ops.current: このきごうりょうりのきごうつくりかたわきごうかんたんです
ops.fix: このりょうりのつくりかたわかんたんです
ops.issue: The kana transcription contains きごう ('symbol') three times where the jp has spaces — a tokenizer artifact (space tokens were assigned reading きごう). A learner reading the kana would read nonsense syllables.

ops.current: konokigouryourinokigoutsukurikatawakigoukantandesu
ops.fix: konoryourinotsukurikatawakantandesu
ops.issue: Same artifact as kana: 'kigou' inserted three times where the jp has spaces. This is not the known punctuation/katakana issue — it adds nonexistent syllables to the sentence's phonetics.

ops.current: きごう
ops.fix: null (space has no reading; or drop the space tokens)
ops.issue: Space-separator tokens were given the reading きごう ('symbol'). Same defect on tokens[4].r and tokens[8].r. This is the root cause of the corrupted kana/romaji; a space has no reading.

ops.current: In the kitchen, first we cut the vegetables.
ops.fix: When cooking, first you cut the vegetables.
ops.issue: 料理 means 'cooking/the act of cooking', not the room 'kitchen' (台所). The natural translation shifts the topic from the activity to a location, contradicting lit_en ('As for cooking') and expl_en itself.

ops.current: Na cozinha, primeiro a gente corta os legumes.
ops.fix: Ao cozinhar, primeiro a gente corta os legumes.
ops.issue: 'Na cozinha' reads as the physical room (台所), but 料理は is the activity of cooking. Contradicts lit_pt ('Quanto a cozinhar') and expl_pt.

ops.current: As for the bird, it, toward the south, goes flying.
ops.fix: The bird (subject), toward the south, goes flying.
ops.issue: The literal mirror uses the topic device ('As for the bird, it...') for 鳥が, but が marks the subject, not a topic — expl_en itself says 鳥が is the subject, and the corpus elsewhere mirrors が as '(subject)' (cf. この大きい荷物が邪魔だ). Blurs the taught は/が distinction.

ops.current: Quanto ao pássaro, ele, em direção ao sul, vai voando.
ops.fix: O pássaro (sujeito), em direção ao sul, vai voando.
ops.issue: Same as lit_en: 'Quanto ao pássaro, ele...' mirrors the が-marked subject with the は-topic device plus a resumptive pronoun, contradicting expl_pt (sujeito) and the corpus convention for が.

ops.current: Quanto a qual trem, sobe (embarca)?
ops.fix: Em qual trem (você) embarca?
ops.issue: The literal mirror topicalizes the interrogative phrase ('Quanto a qual trem'), but どの電車に is the に-complement of 乗る, not a topic (interrogatives cannot be topics). Also broken Portuguese. lit_en correctly renders it without topicalization.

ops.current: As for the length of his talk, I got tired.
ops.fix: By the length of his talk, (I) got tired.
ops.issue: The literal mirror presents 長さに as a topic ('As for...'), but に marks the cause of 疲れた — as expl_en itself states ('points to the cause/target of the tiredness'). The mirror misrepresents the particle structure.

ops.current: Quanto à extensão da conversa dele, (eu) me cansei.
ops.fix: Com a extensão da conversa dele, (eu) me cansei.
ops.issue: Same as lit_en: 'Quanto à' presents the に-marked cause as a topic, contradicting expl_pt ('aponta a causa/alvo do cansaço'). The Quanto-a device belongs to は topics, not に complements.

ops.current: みせでべいをごきろかいました
ops.fix: みせでこめをごきろかいました
ops.issue: Kana transcribes 米 as べい; standalone 米 'rice' is read こめ. The sentence reading is wrong.

ops.current: misedebeiogokirokaimashita
ops.fix: misedekomeogokirokaimashita
ops.issue: Romaji propagates the wrong reading 'bei' for 米; should reflect こめ (kome). Separate from the known punctuation/katakana romaji issue.

ops.current: べい
ops.fix: こめ
ops.issue: 米 meaning 'rice' as a standalone noun is read こめ, not べい. べい is the on-reading used only in compounds (米国, 日米). Reading is wrong in this context.

ops.current: おそふさんわしんぶんをよんでいる
ops.fix: おじいさんわしんぶんをよんでいる
ops.issue: Kana renders お祖父さん as おそふさん, which is not a valid reading; the honorific form is read おじいさん.

ops.current: osofusanwashinbunoyondeiru
ops.fix: ojiisanwashinbunoyondeiru
ops.issue: Romaji propagates the invalid reading 'osofusan'; お祖父さん is read ojiisan. Separate from the known romaji punctuation/katakana issue.

ops.current: そふ
ops.fix: じい
ops.issue: In お祖父さん the reading is おじいさん; 祖父 is read じい here. そふ is the plain humble form and never takes お…さん (おそふさん does not exist).

ops.current: avo (do sexo masculino), vovo
ops.fix: avô (do sexo masculino), vovô
ops.issue: Missing circumflex accents in the Portuguese gloss: 'avo' and 'vovo' should be 'avô' and 'vovô'.

ops.current: That festival is famous in the state.
ops.fix: This festival is famous in the prefecture.
ops.issue: この is proximal 'this', not 'that'; lit_en and expl_en both say 'this'. Also en says 'state' while lit_en/expl_en say 'prefecture' (県) — internally inconsistent.

ops.current: this, that
ops.fix: this
ops.issue: この is glossed 'this, that'; この is strictly proximal ('this'). 'that' belongs to その/あの and teaches a wrong demonstrative fact.

ops.current: From the time of high school, I often went to the library.
ops.fix: At the time of (being) a high school student, I often went to the library.
ops.issue: のとき means 'at the time of', not 'from the time of'; 'From' falsely implies から (ablative) and misteaches the structure.

ops.current: Do tempo de colegial, frequentemente à biblioteca fui.
ops.fix: Na época de colegial, frequentemente à biblioteca fui.
ops.issue: 'Do tempo de colegial' sugere origem (から); のとき significa 'na época de'. Espelho literal impreciso.

ops.current: As for the rain, if it falls, I will be in trouble.
ops.fix: When the rain falls, I will be in trouble.
ops.issue: Literal mirror misrepresents 雨が: が marks the subject, not a topic, so the topic device 'As for the rain' teaches the wrong particle function.

ops.current: Quanto à chuva, se cai, fico em apuros.
ops.fix: Quando a chuva cai, fico em apuros.
ops.issue: Mesmo problema no espelho literal em pt: 'Quanto à chuva' espelha um tópico は, mas a frase usa 雨が (sujeito com が), não tópico.

ops.current: raiz conetiva (連用形) de 買う, base para juntar ます
ops.fix: raiz conectiva (連用形) de 買う, base para juntar ます
ops.issue: pt-BR note uses 'conetiva', the European Portuguese (post-Acordo pt-PT) spelling; Brazilian Portuguese spells it 'conectiva' (cf. same note in other items: 'raiz conectiva').

ops.current: As for becoming spring, the flowers bloom.
ops.fix: When it becomes spring, the flowers open.
ops.issue: Literal mirror misrepresents 春になると as a topic ('As for becoming spring'); there is no は — it is the と conditional clause. Structurally inaccurate mirror.

ops.current: Quanto a tornar-se primavera, as flores se abrem.
ops.fix: Quando se torna primavera, as flores se abrem.
ops.issue: Espelho literal usa 'Quanto a tornar-se primavera' como se houvesse tópico は; a estrutura real é a condicional 〜と. Espelho estruturalmente incorreto.

ops.current: to print
ops.fix: (part of どうして 'why')
ops.issue: Sub-token し of どうして is glossed 'to print' (leaked from the homophone 刷る). It is not a verb here; pt gloss correctly says it is part of どうして. English gloss teaches something false.

ops.current: On the corner of the desk, I hit my head.
ops.fix: On the corner of the table, I hit my head.
ops.issue: テーブル is 'table', not 'desk' (desk = 机); en, pt and lit_pt all correctly say table/mesa.

ops.current: To the friend, he said to come tomorrow.
ops.fix: To the friend, (I) said to come tomorrow.
ops.issue: Subject inconsistency: en, pt and both expl fields render the implicit subject as 'I' ('I told my friend'), but lit_en renders it as 'he said', contradicting the rest of the record.

ops.current: にほんじんわまいにちべいをたべます
ops.fix: にほんじんわまいにちこめをたべます
ops.issue: 米 as a standalone noun (object of 食べる) is read こめ, not the on'yomi べい. The item's own expl_en/expl_pt explicitly say it is read こめ here, so the kana contradicts the explanation.

ops.current: べい
ops.fix: こめ
ops.issue: Token reading for 米 is べい, but standalone 米 meaning 'rice' is read こめ (べい is the compound on'yomi, e.g. 米国). Contradicts the expl fields, which correctly state こめ.

ops.current: nihonjinwamainichibeiotabemasu
ops.fix: nihonjinwamainichikomeotabemasu
ops.issue: Romaji propagates the wrong reading of 米: 'bei' should be 'kome' (standalone 米 = こめ).

ops.current: My younger sister is in middle school.
ops.fix: My younger sister goes to elementary school.
ops.issue: Sense-changing mistranslation: 小学校 is elementary/primary school, not middle school (中学校). The lit_en and token gloss correctly say 'elementary school', so the natural en contradicts the rest of the record.

ops.current: このへやわひろいですきごうそれにあかるいです
ops.fix: このへやわひろいですそれにあかるいです
ops.issue: The literal string きごう ('symbol') was inserted where the sentence has a space between clauses. Reading the kana aloud produces extra syllables not in the sentence.

ops.current: konoheyawahiroidesukigousoreniakaruidesu
ops.fix: konoheyawahiroidesusoreniakaruidesu
ops.issue: Contains 'kigou' (romanization of the spurious きごう reading for the space token). This is extra spoken material, not the known punctuation/katakana issue.

ops.current: きごう
ops.fix: (null — no reading for a space token)
ops.issue: Whitespace separator token was given the reading きごう ('symbol'). A space has no phonetic reading; this is the source of the kana/romaji corruption.

ops.current: bonito, bela
ops.fix: bonito, belo

ops.current: The particle に marks 紙 ('paper') as the place where the action happens.
ops.fix: The particle に marks 紙 ('paper') as the surface where the line ends up (target/place of result) — unlike で, which marks where an action occurs.
ops.full_before: The particle に marks 紙 ('paper') as the place where the action happens. 長い ('long') is an i-adjective that modifies 線 ('line'), and を marks that line as the direct object of the verb 引く ('to pull/draw'), here in the past 引いた. The vocabulary focus is 線.
ops.issue: Wrong particle function: says に marks 紙 as 'the place where the action happens' — that is で's function. With 引く/書く, に marks the surface/target where the result ends up (place of result), a distinction textbooks explicitly teach (紙に書く vs 図書館で勉強する).

ops.issue: Same wrong particle-function claim in Portuguese: に described as 'o lugar onde a ação acontece', which is the function of で. Here に marks the surface/target where the result (the line) remains.

ops.current: はいり

ops.current: I have three older sisters.

ops.issue: First-person translation clashes with お姉さん: honorific kin terms are used for OTHER people's family; one's own older sisters are 姉. As written it teaches learners to call their own sisters お姉さん. Either jp should use 姉 or en/pt should be third person (pt has the same problem).

ops.current: traduzir います por "ter/ter" ("tenho três irmãs")

Em pt-BR fica mais natural traduzir います por "ter/ter" ("tenho três irmãs").
ops.issue: Duplication typo 'ter/ter'; the illustrative quote also drops 'mais velhas' present in both jp sense and the en explanation.

ops.current: é barata e por cima ainda é gostosa

O 〜し aqui acumula elogios: 'é barata e por cima ainda é gostosa'.
ops.issue: Inverted fixed idiom: pt-BR says 'ainda por cima', not 'por cima ainda'.

ops.current: As for the afternoon, a friend is coming.

ops.current: Note that this generated sentence does not carry the final period 。

ops.current: どの is a connective (連体詞) meaning 'which (among several)'

ops.issue: 'connective' is the wrong English label for 連体詞: a connective is 接続詞. 連体詞 is an adnominal / pre-noun adjectival. The kanji term and the described function are correct.

ops.issue: 'conetivo' is European-Portuguese spelling (BR: 'conectivo'), and 'conectivo' is the wrong term anyway: 連体詞 is um pré-nominal/adnominal; conectivo corresponds to 接続詞. Function is otherwise described correctly.

ops.current: The sentence uses 〜になる ('to turn into/become') twice.
ops.fix: The sentence uses the verb なる ('to turn into/become') twice.
ops.full_before: The sentence uses 〜になる ('to turn into/become') twice. In 晩になる (ばんになる), the noun 晩 (night) takes に and 'reaches/turns into night'; the と right after the verb creates the condition 'when/whenever'. The second part, 涼しくなる, uses 涼しい (すずしい, cool) in the form 涼しく + なる to indicate a change of state: 'it gets cool'. The focus is the vocabulary 晩 (night).
ops.issue: False grammar-form claim: the sentence does not use 〜になる twice. 晩になる is noun+に+なる, but 涼しくなる is the i-adjective adverbial form 涼しく + なる (〜くなる), not になる. The rest of the paragraph derives 涼しく correctly, contradicting the opening claim.

ops.current: A frase usa duas vezes 〜になる ('virar/ficar').

A segunda parte, 涼しくなる, usa 涼しい (すずしい, fresco) na forma 涼しく + なる para indicar mudança de estado: 'fica fresco'. O foco é o vocabulário 晩 (noite).
ops.issue: Same false claim as expl_en: afirma que a frase usa 〜になる duas vezes, mas 涼しくなる é 〜くなる (adjetivo-い na forma adverbial + なる), não になる. Contradiz a própria explicação que segue.

ops.issue: The whitespace tokens were assigned the reading きごう ('symbol') and it leaked into the sentence-level kana twice. The phonetic transcription contains syllables that are not in the sentence.

ops.current: ashitakigouhonokigoukau
ops.fix: ashitahonokau
ops.issue: Same きごう leak as kana: 'kigou' appears twice in the romanization from the space tokens. Not the known punctuation/katakana issue — these are extra invented syllables.

ops.current: きごう
ops.fix: (null — whitespace has no reading)
ops.issue: Whitespace token (surface = ' ') has reading きごう ('symbol'), a tokenizer artifact. Same defect at tokens[4].r. Space tokens should have null/empty reading (or be dropped).

ops.current: でわきごうまたあす
ops.fix: でわまたあした
ops.issue: Two defects: (1) きごう leaked from the space token into the kana; (2) 明日 in the everyday farewell また明日 is read あした, not the formal/literary あす.

ops.current: dewakigoumataasu
ops.fix: dewamataashita
ops.issue: Mirrors the kana defects: 'kigou' inserted from the space token, and 明日 romanized as 'asu' instead of 'ashita' (the natural reading in the farewell また明日).

ops.current: きごう
ops.fix: (null — whitespace has no reading)
ops.issue: Whitespace token (surface = ' ') has reading きごう ('symbol'), a tokenizer artifact. Should be null/empty (or the token dropped).

ops.current: あす
ops.fix: あした
ops.issue: 明日 read as あす. In the set colloquial farewell では、また明日 natives say あした; あす is formal/newsy and unnatural here. en/pt/expl all treat it as an everyday farewell.

ops.current: A cada um dia(de intervalo), à academia vou.
ops.fix: A cada um dia (de intervalo), à academia vou.
ops.issue: Missing space before the parenthesis: 'dia(de intervalo)'.

ops.current: As for the bed, on the left side, there's a window.
ops.fix: On the left side of the bed, there's a window.
ops.issue: Structural mirror is wrong: ベッドの is a genitive inside the NP ベッドの左側 ('the left side of the bed'), not a topic. Rendering it 'As for the bed' splits the NP and falsely implies a は-topic; there is no は in the sentence.

ops.current: Quanto à cama, no lado esquerdo, há janela.
ops.fix: No lado esquerdo da cama, há janela.
ops.issue: Same as lit_en: 'Quanto à cama' treats the genitive ベッドの as a topic, breaking the NP ベッドの左側 and teaching a false structure (the 'Quanto a' device is reserved for は-topics; this sentence has none).

ops.current: あめのひわのきのもとでまちます
ops.fix: あめのひわのきのしたでまちます
ops.issue: Kana transcribes 軒の下 as のきのもと; the correct in-context reading is のきのした (physical 'under the eaves').

ops.current: もと
ops.fix: した
ops.issue: 下 in 軒の下 (physical location 'under the eaves') is read した, not もと. もと (下/元) is used for abstract 'under the auspices of' (法の下, 青空の下 in set phrases); the standard reading for sheltering under the eaves is のきのした (cf. 軒下 のきした).

ops.current: amenohiwanokinomotodemachimasu
ops.fix: amenohiwanokinoshitademachimasu
ops.issue: Romaji carries the same wrong reading for 軒の下 ('nokinomoto' instead of 'nokinoshita').

ops.current: With a match, as for the fire, I lit (it).
ops.fix: With a match, the fire (I) lit.
ops.issue: The topic-marking device 'as for' is applied to 火を, an を-marked direct object, not a は topic. This misrepresents the structure the literal field is supposed to mirror (the expl itself says を marks the object). Corpus convention elsewhere reserves 'as for/Quanto a' for は.

ops.current: Com fósforo, quanto a fogo, (eu) acendi.
ops.fix: Com fósforo, o fogo (eu) acendi.
ops.issue: 'Quanto a fogo' applies the は-topic teaching device to 火を, an object marked by を. The literal mirror should show 火 as object, not topic (compare item sent:gen-a7f6f5095b68, where a fronted を object correctly avoids 'Quanto a').

ops.current: As for Africa, I want to try going there.
ops.fix: To Africa, (I) want to try going.
ops.issue: 'As for Africa' renders アフリカに as if it were a は topic; に here is the destination particle and there is no topic in the sentence. The literal mirror teaches a structure that is not present.

ops.current: Quanto à África, indo, quero experimentar (ir).
ops.fix: Para a África, quero experimentar ir.
ops.issue: 'Quanto à África' applies the は-topic device to アフリカに (destination particle に); the sentence has no topic. The literal mirror should show the destination relation.

ops.current: Quanto às letras, de modo bonito, escrever.
ops.fix: As letras (objeto), de modo bonito, escrever.
ops.issue: 'Quanto a' is the course's mirror for topic は, but 字 is marked by を (direct object). The literal rendering wrongly teaches 字を as a topicalized noun; every other 'Quanto a' in this batch mirrors は.

ops.current: Também (また), depois (後で), para aí/para você (そちらに) telefono (forma polida).
ops.fix: De novo (また), depois (後で), para aí/para você (そちらに) telefono (forma polida).
ops.issue: In また後で電話します, また means 'de novo' (again), as both natural translations render it; 'Também' shifts the sense to 'in addition (to something else)'. lit_en 'Also,' has the same problem and should read 'Again,'.

ops.current: Quanto àquela pessoa, (ela) é realmente odiosa (para mim).
ops.fix: Aquela pessoa (sujeito) é realmente odiosa (para mim).
ops.issue: あの人 is marked by が (subject/target of the emotive adjective), not topic は. Applying the 'Quanto a' topic device to a が-marked noun blurs the は/が distinction; the parallel が sentence (祖母が…) correctly avoids it.

ops.current: Quanto ao trem, suavemente, na plataforma, parou.
ops.fix: lit_pt: "O trem (sujeito), suavemente, na plataforma, parou." — and apply the same fix to lit_en: "The train (subject) stopped smoothly at the platform."
ops.issue: 電車 is marked by が (subject), not topic は, yet the literal uses the topic device 'Quanto ao' (and lit_en uses 'As for the train'). This teaches が as if it were は; the expl correctly calls 電車が the subject.

ops.current: えきまでじゅうふんくらいかかる
ops.fix: えきまでじゅっぷんくらいかかる
ops.issue: 十分 meaning 'ten minutes' is read じゅっぷん (or じっぷん), never じゅうふん. The record's own expl_en/expl_pt state じゅっぷん/じっぷん, contradicting the kana. Romaji 'juufun' needs the matching fix (juppun).

ops.current: じゅう
ops.fix: じゅっ
ops.issue: Reading of 十 in 十分 'ten minutes' geminates: じゅっ (juppun), not じゅう. Consistent with the fix to kana and tokens[3].r.

ops.current: ふん
ops.fix: ぷん
ops.issue: 分 in the duration reading after 十 is ぷん (じゅっぷん), not ふん. The expl itself gives じゅっぷん/じっぷん.

ops.current: As for the sea's sand, it was very hot.
ops.fix: As for the sea's sand, it was very warm.
ops.issue: 温かい means 'warm', not 'hot' (that is 熱い). The token gloss says '(was) warm, lukewarm' and en says 'really warm'; 'very hot' in the literal field misteaches the 温かい/熱い contrast.

ops.current: As for the class break, as for him, he was quiet the whole time.
ops.fix: During the class period, as for him, he was quiet the whole time.
ops.issue: 授業の間 means 'during the class' (the duration of the class itself), not 'the class break'. 'Break' would be 休み時間/合間. Contradicts the (correct) expl_en, which says 間 marks the whole duration of the class.

ops.current: Quanto ao intervalo da aula, quanto a ele, o tempo todo estava quieto.
ops.fix: Durante o período da aula, quanto a ele, o tempo todo estava quieto.
ops.issue: 'Intervalo da aula' in pt-BR means the recess/break between classes; 授業の間 here means 'durante a aula' (a duração da própria aula). Teaches 間 = intervalo, contradicting the correct expl_pt.

ops.current: There are two overlapping topics: 今日は ('as for today') situates the time, and 風が points to the wind as the subject
ops.fix: 今日は ('as for today') sets the time as the topic, and 風が marks the wind as the subject that is 涼しい (cool/pleasant).
ops.full_before: There are two overlapping topics: 今日は ('as for today') situates the time, and 風が points to the wind as the subject that is 涼しい (cool/pleasant). です makes the sentence polite and ね at the end seeks agreement ('right?'). Note that 涼しい is the pleasant 'cool', not the unpleasant 'cold'.
ops.issue: 'Two overlapping topics' mislabels 風が: が marks the subject, not a topic. The sentence itself then calls it the subject, so the opening claim is internally inconsistent and blurs the は-topic vs が-subject distinction the course teaches.

ops.current: Há dois tópicos sobrepostos: 今日は ('quanto a hoje') situa o tempo, e 風が aponta o vento como sujeito
ops.fix: 今日は ('quanto a hoje') marca o tópico de tempo, e 風が aponta o vento como sujeito que é 涼しい (fresco/agradável).
ops.full_before: Há dois tópicos sobrepostos: 今日は ('quanto a hoje') situa o tempo, e 風が aponta o vento como sujeito que é 涼しい (fresco/agradável). です deixa a frase polida e ね no fim busca concordância ('né?'). Note que 涼しい é o 'fresco' agradável, não o 'frio' desagradável.
ops.issue: 'Dois tópicos sobrepostos' rotula 風が como tópico; が marca o sujeito, não um tópico. Mesma inconsistência interna da versão em inglês (a própria frase depois chama 風 de sujeito).

ops.current: tema (circunstancia de tempo)
ops.fix: tema (circunstância de tempo)
ops.issue: Missing accent in Portuguese: 'circunstancia' should be 'circunstância'.

ops.current: Antes de (de) sair, a eletricidade/luz (を), apago.
ops.fix: Antes de sair, a eletricidade/luz (を), apago.
ops.issue: Duplicated 'de' in 'Antes de (de) sair' — reads as a typo; the parenthetical adds nothing structural (まえに is already mirrored by 'Antes de').

ops.current: As for the film, there's none left.
ops.fix: The film (subject), already there is none.
ops.issue: The topic-mirror device 'As for...' is applied to a が-marked subject; the sentence has no は topic. This contradicts expl_en (which correctly says が marks the subject) and blurs the は/が distinction the lit field exists to teach.

ops.current: Quanto ao filme, já não existe.
ops.fix: O filme (sujeito), já não existe.
ops.issue: 'Quanto ao filme' mirrors a は topic, but フィルム is marked by が (subject); expl_pt itself says が marks the sujeito. The literal mirror misrepresents the particle structure.

ops.current: けんきゅうしつのどあがひらいている
ops.fix: けんきゅうしつのどあがあいている
ops.issue: ドアが開いている describing the resulting open state of a door is normally read あいている (開く=あく). ひらいている is the marked reading (flowers, books, doors spreading open) and sounds unnatural here; あく is also the N4-appropriate reading.

ops.current: ひらい
ops.fix: あい
ops.issue: Same reading issue as the kana field: for a door's open state, 開い is read あい (from あく), not ひらい. Romaji would also need the corresponding fix (aiteiru).

ops.current: bem (forma de いい/よい em よくない = não é bom)
ops.fix: bom
ops.issue: pt gloss of いい is garbled, copied from a negative sentence: it glosses 'bem' and references よくない, which does not occur here. The en gloss is 'good'; in 〜といいです the gloss should be 'bom'.

ops.current: No rio, ao peixe pesquei.
ops.fix: No rio, o peixe (を) pesquei.
ops.issue: 'ao peixe' (a + o) marks an indirect/dative object in Portuguese, misrepresenting the accusative を; house style elsewhere shows the particle in parentheses instead.

ops.current: Estou bem na hora de sair agora mesmo.
ops.fix: Estou de saída agora mesmo.
ops.issue: 'Estou bem na hora de sair' is off-idiom in pt-BR ('bem na hora' = 'just in time', not 'about to'); awkward rendering of 〜るところだ.

ops.current: The clerk, as for the product, did me the favor of exchanging (it).
ops.fix: The clerk, the product [object], did me the favor of exchanging (it).
ops.issue: Literal mirror renders を-marked object 商品を as 'as for the product', the device reserved for topic は. This misteaches を as a topic marker in the structural field.

ops.current: O atendente, quanto ao produto, fez-me o favor de trocar.
ops.fix: O atendente, o produto [objeto], me fez o favor de trocar.
ops.issue: Same mis-mapping: 'quanto ao produto' applies the topic-は device to the object particle を. Also 'fez-me' is Portugal-style enclisis; pt-BR uses proclisis ('me fez').

ops.current: Quanto a aquela pessoa (が), novo diretor é.
ops.fix: Aquela pessoa (が), novo diretor é.
ops.issue: Uses the topic device 'Quanto a' for subject particle が, directly contradicting expl_pt, which stresses が (not は) marks identification/focus here. Also missing crase: 'a aquela' should be 'àquela' if kept.

ops.current: That person is the new director.
ops.fix: That person is the new principal.
ops.issue: 校長 rendered as 'director' (calque of pt 'diretor'); in en-US a school 校長 is 'principal', as the main en field itself uses. Inconsistent and misleading in English.

ops.current: I study about two hours... I mean, roughly one hour a day.
ops.fix: I study about an hour every day.
ops.issue: Corrupted translation with a spurious self-correction ('about two hours... I mean') that contradicts the JP. 一時間くらい means simply 'about one hour'; nothing in the sentence supports 'two hours' or a repair.

ops.current: Eu estudo umas duas horas... digo, mais ou menos uma hora por dia.
ops.fix: Eu estudo mais ou menos uma hora por dia.
ops.issue: Same corruption as en: invents 'umas duas horas... digo' — a false start/self-correction absent from the JP. 一時間くらい is just 'mais ou menos uma hora'.

ops.current: Quanto a roupa (sujeito), com lama (meio), sujou-se (acabou fazendo, passado).
ops.fix: Quanto à roupa (sujeito), com lama (meio), sujou-se (acabou fazendo, passado).
ops.issue: Missing crase: 'Quanto a roupa' should be 'Quanto à roupa' (the bank writes 'Quanto à biblioteca', 'Quanto ao estacionamento' elsewhere).

ops.current: ななかにびょういんえいくよていだ
ops.fix: なのかにびょういんえいくよていだ
ops.issue: 7日 (day 7 of the month) is read なのか, not ななか. The token note in the same item even states '七日 = なのか', contradicting the kana field.

ops.current: なな
ops.fix: なの
ops.issue: Reading なな for ７ is wrong in the date word 7日 = なのか (irregular date reading). With 日 = か, the numeral part must read なの.

ops.current: nanakanibyouineikuyoteida
ops.fix: nanokanibyouineikuyoteida
ops.issue: Romaji mirrors the wrong kana reading ななか; 7日 is nanoka.

ops.current: and (to be)
ops.fix: is (to be)
ops.issue: だ is the copula 'is/to be', not the conjunction 'and'. The English gloss 'and (to be)' teaches a false equivalence (likely propagated from the 'e/é' typo in lit_pt).

ops.current: No dia 7, ao hospital ir, e plano.
ops.fix: No dia 7, ao hospital ir, é plano.
ops.issue: Missing accent: 'e plano' reads as 'and plan'; the copula だ should be rendered 'é plano' (cf. lit_en 'is (my) plan').

ops.current: dia(do mes); contador de dias
ops.fix: dia (do mês); contador de dias
ops.issue: Missing space and accent in the Portuguese gloss: 'dia(do mes)' should be 'dia (do mês)'.

ops.current: predicado nominal (nucleo de 〜予定だ)
ops.fix: predicado nominal (núcleo de 〜予定だ)
ops.issue: Missing accent: 'nucleo' should be 'núcleo' (other items in the bank consistently use the accented form).

ops.current: copula
ops.fix: cópula
ops.issue: Missing accent: 'copula' should be 'cópula' (cf. 'cópula (verbo de ligação polido)' elsewhere in this batch). The pt-BR note 'da copula' has the same accent error.

ops.current: (polite copula/auxiliary)
ops.fix: (politeness auxiliary)
ops.issue: ます is glossed as a 'polite copula'; it is a politeness auxiliary, never a copula (compare correct glosses in sibling items: '(politeness marker)', '(polite auxiliary)'). Mislabels a core grammar term for learners.

ops.current: (cópula/auxiliar polido)
ops.fix: (auxiliar de polidez)
ops.issue: Same defect in pt: ます glossed as 'cópula'; ます não é cópula, é auxiliar de polidez (o role do próprio token diz 'auxiliar de polidez').

ops.current: このみせわやすいきごうそれにりょうりもおいしい
ops.fix: このみせわやすいそれにりょうりもおいしい
ops.issue: The full-width space in jp was transcribed as きごう ('symbol' — a tokenizer artifact), inserting syllables that are not pronounced. Remove きごう (optionally keep the space itself).

ops.current: きごう
ops.fix: Set r to null; if the schema requires a non-null string, use "　" (the space itself) and keep kana/romaji free of きごう/kigou.
ops.issue: The space token 「　」 was given the reading きごう ('symbol'), which is the tokenizer's label, not a pronunciation. A space has no reading.

ops.current: konomisewayasuikigousoreniryourimooishii
ops.fix: konomisewayasuisoreniryourimooishii
ops.issue: Romaji contains 'kigou', the spurious reading of the space token; it is not part of the sentence's pronunciation (distinct from the known punctuation-in-romaji issue).

ops.current: りんごをむいつください
ops.fix: りんごをむっつください
ops.issue: 六つ is read むっつ, not むいつ. The item's own expl_en/expl_pt correctly state 'read むっつ', so the kana contradicts the explanation and teaches a wrong reading.

ops.current: むい
ops.fix: むっ
ops.issue: Token 六 (before counter つ) has reading むい; in 六つ the segment is むっ (full word むっつ).

ops.current: ringoomuitsukudasai
ops.fix: ringoomuttsukudasai
ops.issue: Romaji reflects the wrong reading むいつ; 六つ is muttsu.

ops.current: modificador (núcleo do tópico)
ops.fix: modificador do tópico (liga-se ao núcleo 道具 com の)
ops.issue: Role of 掃除 is self-contradictory: labeled 'modificador' but the parenthetical calls it 'núcleo do tópico'. The head (núcleo) is 道具 (whose role is 'tópico'); 掃除 only modifies it via の.

ops.current: Quanto à frente da estação (の前に), policial (が) existe.
ops.fix: Na frente da estação (の前に), policial (が) existe.
ops.issue: Locative phrase 駅の前に (marked by に, no は in the sentence) rendered with the topic device 'Quanto à frente da estação' (lit_en 'As for in front of the station'), implying topicalization. The identical structure in sent:gen-b4abb24cc60b is rendered as a plain locative.

ops.current: Quanto ao advogado (が), foi para a entrevista/audiência (接見に行きました).
ops.fix: O advogado (が, sujeito) foi para a entrevista (接見に行きました).
ops.issue: が-marked subject rendered with the topic device 'Quanto ao advogado (が)' (lit_en: 'As for the lawyer (が)'), implying が marks a topic. Corpus convention renders が as '(sujeito)' (cf. sent:gen-b3f7aec99b37 lit_pt). Blurs the は/が distinction the course teaches.

ops.current: Todo mês, à mãe, quanto a carta, (eu) escrevo.
ops.fix: Todo mês, à mãe, carta (objeto), (eu) escrevo.
ops.issue: 手紙を is the direct object marked by を (the expl itself says 'objeto marcado por を'), but lit_pt renders it with the topic device 'quanto a carta' (lit_en likewise 'as for a letter'), teaching that を marks a topic. Corpus convention reserves 'Quanto a' for は.

ops.current: raiz conetiva (連用形) de ある, usada antes de ます
ops.fix: raiz conectiva (連用形) de ある, usada antes de ます
ops.issue: pt-BR note on the あり token uses 'conetiva' — European-Portuguese post-AO90 spelling (or typo); pt-BR requires 'conectiva', as used in the same construction in sent:gen-b3f0ef0078d7 ('raiz conectiva').

ops.current: Quanto à comemoração da entrada (na escola), (eu a) recebi.
ops.fix: A comemoração da entrada (na escola) (objeto), (eu a) recebi.
ops.issue: お祝いを is the を-marked direct object (expl: 'objeto direto marcado por を'), but lit_pt renders it with the topic device 'Quanto à comemoração', misrepresenting を as a topic marker. Also structurally inconsistent with lit_en, which shows no topic.

ops.current: caro (forma て: 'mesmo que seja caro')
ops.fix: caro
ops.issue: Stray parenthetical claims 高い is in te-form meaning 'mesmo que seja caro' (concessive 高くても). The token is in dictionary form (the note itself says 'forma de dicionário'), and the en gloss is just 'expensive'. Copy-paste contamination teaching a false conjugation.

ops.current: ははのたんじょうびわこんげつのいちれいにちだ
ops.fix: ははのたんじょうびわこんげつのとおかだ
ops.issue: １０日 (day 10 of the month) must be read とおか, not いちれいにち (digit-by-digit 'one-zero' reading, which is not Japanese).

ops.current: hahanotanjoubiwakongetsunoichireinichida
ops.fix: hahanotanjoubiwakongetsunotookada
ops.issue: Romaji carries the same wrong reading of １０日: 'ichireinichi' instead of 'tooka'. (Separate from the known punctuation/katakana issue.)

ops.current: いちれい
ops.fix: とお
ops.issue: Token １０ in １０日 is read とお (as in とおか), never いちれい.

ops.current: にち
ops.fix: か
ops.issue: Token 日 in １０日 (とおか) is read か here, not にち; にち only fits readings like じゅういちにち, not the irregular とおか.

ops.current: Quanto ao aniversário da mãe, é o dia 10 de este mês.
ops.fix: Quanto ao aniversário da mãe, é o dia 10 deste mês.
ops.issue: 'de este mês' violates the obligatory Portuguese contraction; standard pt-BR requires 'deste mês' (the natural pt field itself uses 'deste').

ops.current: ちーずをさんひゃくぐらむかいました
ops.fix: ちーずをさんびゃくぐらむかいました
ops.issue: 三百 is read さんびゃく (rendaku after ん: sanbyaku), not さんひゃく.

ops.current: chi-zuosanhyakuguramukaimashita
ops.fix: chi-zuosanbyakuguramukaimashita
ops.issue: Romaji carries the same wrong reading: 'sanhyaku' should be 'sanbyaku'. (Separate from the known katakana/punctuation issue.)

ops.current: さんひゃく
ops.fix: さんびゃく
ops.issue: Token 三百 reading must be さんびゃく, not さんひゃく.

ops.current: As for cheese (を), I bought three hundred grams.
ops.fix: Cheese (を), three hundred grams, I bought.
ops.issue: 'As for' is the topic (は) teaching device, but チーズ is marked by を as direct object; the literal mirror wrongly presents an object as a topic.

ops.current: Quanto a queijo (を), trezentos gramas comprei.
ops.fix: Queijo (を), trezentos gramas, comprei.
ops.issue: 'Quanto a' is the topic (は) device, but チーズを is a direct object; the literal mirror misrepresents を as topicalization.

ops.current: When I called, he came right over to help me.
ops.fix: When I called, he came right over.
ops.issue: 'to help me' adds a purpose absent from the Japanese; 来てくれた only says he kindly came (the coming itself is the favor), not that he came in order to help.

ops.current: Quando liguei, ele veio na hora pra me ajudar.
ops.fix: Quando liguei, ele veio na hora.
ops.issue: 'pra me ajudar' acrescenta uma finalidade que não está no japonês; 来てくれた indica apenas que ele veio como favor, não que veio para ajudar.

ops.current: forma まし do auxiliar ます, base para a partícula た
ops.fix: forma まし do auxiliar ます, base para o auxiliar た
ops.issue: た is called a 'particle' ('base para a partícula た' / 'base for the particle た'); た is an auxiliary (助動詞), and the same record's た token correctly labels it 'auxiliar de passado'. Terminology error in both note languages.

ops.current: auxiliar passivo れる (verbo do grupo 1), liga-se a 歌わ
ops.fix: auxiliar passivo れる (conjuga como verbo do grupo 2/ichidan), liga-se a 歌わ

ops.current: The vocabulary focus is 厚い in the sense of 'thick/thick (objects)', distinct from 熱い 'hot'.

The vocabulary focus is 厚い in the sense of 'thick/thick (objects)', distinct from 熱い 'hot'.

ops.current: The core is 看護婦になる ('to become a nurse')

All of this is quoted by the particle と and embedded in 思っている ('to be thinking'), the 〜ている form indicating a continuous state/thought. Together, it expresses a wish the person has been nurturing.

Tudo isso é citado pela partícula と e encaixado em 思っている ('estar pensando'), a forma 〜ている que indica um estado/pensamento contínuo. Junto, expressa um desejo que a pessoa vem nutrindo.

ops.current: Fala com palavras simples, por favor.

ops.current: The order is always place → object → verb.
ops.fix: The most common order is place → object → verb, but the two can swap as long as the verb stays last.
ops.full_before: A dictionary-style sentence (verb in dictionary form, no explicit subject). The particle に marks 壁 (wall) as the place/target where the action fixes, を marks ポスター (poster) as the direct object, and 張る (to stick, to put up) is the main verb. The order is always place → object → verb.
ops.issue: Claims word order is 'always' place → object → verb. Japanese pre-verbal order is flexible: ポスターを壁に張る is equally grammatical and common. Teaching an absolute rule that does not exist misleads learners.

ops.current: A ordem é sempre lugar → objeto → verbo.
ops.fix: A ordem mais comum é lugar → objeto → verbo, mas eles podem trocar de posição desde que o verbo fique no final.
ops.full_before: Frase no estilo de dicionário (verbo na forma de dicionário, sem sujeito explícito). A partícula に marca 壁 (parede) como o lugar/alvo onde a ação se fixa, を marca ポスター (pôster) como o objeto direto, e 張る (colar, pregar) é o verbo principal. A ordem é sempre lugar → objeto → verbo.
ops.issue: Same false absolute rule as expl_en: 'sempre lugar → objeto → verbo'. Japanese allows ポスターを壁に張る; only the verb-final position is fixed.

ops.full_before: Adjective + object を past-tense verb structure: 新しい (new) is an い-adjective qualifying 箸, を marks the direct object, and 買った is the past form of 買う (to buy). The vocabulary focus is 箸; 買った is formed by 買っ (stem in て form) plus the auxiliary た that indicates the past.
ops.issue: expl_en calls 買っ a 'stem in て form' while expl_pt (and the token note) correctly call it the た-form stem — the two language versions disagree on the form name for the same segment.

ops.current: このくにわべいをゆしゅつしている

ops.current: The implicit contrastive が is all contained in the word けれど.
ops.fix: けれど plays the same contrastive role as the conjunction が ('but').
ops.full_before: The sentence has two parts linked by the conjunction けれど ('but, however'). The first is 勉強した ('I studied', past form of 勉強する). The second brings the topic テストは ('as for the test') followed by the past adjective 難しかった ('was hard'). The implicit contrastive が is all contained in the word けれど.
ops.issue: Claims 'the implicit contrastive が is all contained in けれど', implying a hidden/omitted particle. No が is omitted: けれど is itself the contrastive conjunction, equivalent to conjunctive が. Misleading for beginners.

ops.current: O が implícito de contraste fica todo na palavra けれど.
ops.fix: けれど faz aqui o mesmo papel contrastivo da conjunção が ('mas').
ops.full_before: A frase tem duas partes ligadas pela conjunção けれど ('mas, porém'). A primeira é 勉強した ('estudei', forma passada de 勉強する). A segunda traz o tópico テストは ('quanto à prova') seguido do adjetivo no passado 難しかった ('estava difícil'). O が implícito de contraste fica todo na palavra けれど.
ops.issue: Same misleading claim as expl_en: implies an omitted contrastive が hidden inside けれど; けれど is itself the contrastive conjunction, it does not contain an implicit が.

ops.current: É a forma じゃない passada para o passado (ない → なかった + た).
ops.fix: É a forma じゃない passada para o passado (ない → なかっ + た = なかった).
ops.full_before: A frase segue o padrão [tópico] は [substantivo] じゃなかった. O tópico きのう (ontem) é marcado por は. O alvo じゃなかった é o passado negativo casual da cópula, usado com substantivos: 休み (folga/descanso) + じゃなかった = 'não foi folga'. É a forma じゃない passada para o passado (ない → なかった + た).
ops.issue: Garbled derivation: '(ない → なかった + た)' reads as なかった + another た. The English version has the correct '(ない → なかった)'.

ops.current: Here the predicate is not an い-adjective but a noun (人気) used adjectivally, so it takes です rather than informal だ.
ops.fix: The predicate is the noun 人気 used adjectivally; in this polite sentence it closes with です (plain style would be 人気だ).
ops.full_before: This sentence applies the superlative 〜のなかで〜がいちばん〜, 'among X, Y is the most 〜', in polite register (it ends in です). スポーツの中で ('among sports') is the set; サッカーが marks the winner with が; 一番人気 ('the most popular') uses 一番 with the noun 人気 ('popularity'), and です closes it politely. Here the predicate is not an い-adjective but a noun (人気) used adjectivally, so it takes です rather than informal だ.
ops.issue: 'so it takes です rather than informal だ' wrongly implies noun predicates require です; informal 人気だ is perfectly grammatical — です vs だ is register, not noun-vs-adjective. い-adjectives also take です in polite speech.

ops.current: Aqui o predicado não é um adjetivo い, mas um nome (人気) usado de modo adjetival, então leva です em vez de だ informal.
ops.fix: O predicado é o substantivo 人気 usado de modo adjetival; no registro polido fecha com です (no informal seria 人気だ).
ops.full_before: Esta frase aplica o superlativo 〜のなかで〜がいちばん〜, 'dentre X, Y é o mais 〜', em registro polido (termina em です). スポーツの中で ('dentre os esportes') é o conjunto; サッカーが marca o vencedor com が; 一番人気 ('o mais popular') usa 一番 com o substantivo 人気 ('popularidade'), e です fecha de forma educada. Aqui o predicado não é um adjetivo い, mas um nome (人気) usado de modo adjetival, então leva です em vez de だ informal.
ops.issue: Same false implication as expl_en: 'então leva です em vez de だ informal' teaches that a noun predicate forces です over だ; informally 人気だ is fine — the choice is register, not word class.

ops.current: Lava o copo, por favor.
ops.fix: Lave o copo, por favor.
ops.issue: Register mismatch: polite 〜てください rendered with informal imperative 'Lava'; the corpus renders てください with neutral-polite imperative elsewhere (e.g. 'Abaixe o volume da música, por favor').

ops.current: At the library, I asked the staff member for the way.

ops.current: As in item 1, the tokenizer split でも into で+も, but they form a single conjunction.
ops.fix: Although the breakdown shows で + も separately, でも here is a single conjunction ('but').
ops.full_before: There are two short sentences in the casual register (no です/ます). The first, 疲れた, is the past of 疲れる (to get tired): 疲れ + た. The second begins with でも (but) and ends in 楽しかった, the past of the い-adjective 楽しい (fun). The target is the contrast でも (but) at the start of the second sentence. As in item 1, the tokenizer split でも into で+も, but they form a single conjunction.
ops.issue: Learner-facing explanation leaks authoring internals: 'As in item 1' references a nonexistent item and 'the tokenizer' is internal tooling. Confusing in standalone lesson content.

ops.current: Como no item 1, o tokenizador separou でも em で+も, mas eles formam uma única conjunção.

ops.full_before: São duas frases curtas em registro casual. A primeira, 疲れた, é o passado de 疲れる (cansar-se): 疲れ + た. A segunda começa com でも (mas) e termina em 楽しかった, passado do い-adjetivo 楽しい (divertido). O alvo é o contraste でも (mas) no início da segunda frase. Como no item 1, o tokenizador separou でも em で+も, mas eles formam uma única conjunção.
ops.issue: Same leaked authoring artifact in the pt version: 'Como no item 1, o tokenizador...' references a nonexistent item and internal tooling.

ops.current: where the particle こと turns the verb 撮る ('to take/photograph') into something nominal
ops.fix: where the nominalizer こと (a formal noun) turns the verb 撮る ('to take/photograph') into something nominal
ops.full_before: This is an 'A は B だ' type sentence (A is B). The topic is 私の趣味 ('my hobby'), marked by は. The predicate is 写真を撮ること, where the particle こと turns the verb 撮る ('to take/photograph') into something nominal ('the act of taking photos'), allowing it to function as a noun after だ. In English the こと is not translated literally; it simply becomes the infinitive 'to take photos'.
ops.issue: Wrong word-class claim: こと is not a particle; it is a nominalizer (formal noun 形式名詞). Teaching it as a particle is a false grammar fact.

ops.current: onde a partícula こと transforma o verbo 撮る ('tirar/fotografar') em algo nominal
ops.fix: onde o nominalizador こと (substantivo formal) transforma o verbo 撮る ('tirar/fotografar') em algo nominal
ops.full_before: Esta é uma frase do tipo 'A は B だ' (A é B). O tópico é 私の趣味 ('meu hobby'), marcado por は. O predicado é 写真を撮ること, onde a partícula こと transforma o verbo 撮る ('tirar/fotografar') em algo nominal ('o ato de tirar fotos'), permitindo que ele funcione como substantivo após だ. Em pt-BR o こと não se traduz literalmente; vira simplesmente o infinitivo 'tirar fotos'.
ops.issue: Mesma afirmação errada: こと não é partícula; é um nominalizador (substantivo formal 形式名詞). O próprio token o rotula corretamente como 'nominalizador'.

ops.current: In English, 'there is money' sounds natural as 'have money', hence 'there's no money in the wallet'.

ops.current: to like / pleasant

ops.current: gostar de / agradável

ops.current: marked by に, which indicates where the action happens
ops.fix: marked by に, which indicates the surface where the name ends up (the target of the writing)
ops.full_before: The place is given by 紙の裏 ('the back of the paper'), marked by に, which indicates where the action happens. 名前 ('name') is the object marked by を, and the request is formed with the て-form of the verb 書く ('to write') + ください ('please'). The target is the vocabulary 裏 (back/reverse side).
ops.issue: Claims に 'indicates where the action happens' — that is で's function. With 書く, に marks the surface/target where the name ends up (point of arrival), a core に-vs-で distinction; as written it teaches the wrong particle rule.

ops.current: marcado por に, que indica onde a ação acontece

ops.issue: Mirrors the same wrong claim: に 'indica onde a ação acontece' describes で, not に. Here に marca a superfície/destino onde o nome fica escrito.

ops.current: the generic counter つ (for small, rounded objects)
ops.fix: the generic counter つ (used for objects in general)

ops.issue: Wrong counter description: つ is the all-purpose generic counter for objects; 'for small, rounded objects' describes 個, not つ. The parenthetical teaches a false restriction.

ops.current: a quantia é o que 'foi sorteada'
ops.fix: a quantia é o que 'foi sorteado'

O alvo (vocabulário de números grandes) aparece em 三億 (trezentos milhões).
ops.issue: Agreement error: relative 'o que' requires masculine default agreement, so 'o que foi sorteado', not 'sorteada'.

ops.current: Pensa nisso com mais seriedade, por favor.

ops.current: affectionate suffix (-ie, masc.)

ops.current: 少し is an adverb ('a little') that intensifies the i-adjective 難しい
ops.fix: 少し is an adverb ('a little') that moderates the degree of the i-adjective 難しい
ops.full_before: 日本語の文法 is a noun phrase where の links 日本語 (Japanese language) to 文法 (grammar), forming 'Japanese grammar'. は marks this whole group as the topic. 少し is an adverb ('a little') that intensifies the i-adjective 難しい (difficult), which closes the sentence as the predicate.
ops.issue: 少し is a downtoner ('a little'); it moderates the degree of 難しい, it does not intensify it. 'Intensifies' states the opposite of the adverb's function.

ops.current: 少し é um advérbio ('um pouco') que intensifica o adjetivo-い 難しい
ops.fix: 少し é um advérbio ('um pouco') que atenua o grau do adjetivo-い 難しい
ops.full_before: 日本語の文法 é um sintagma nominal onde の liga 日本語 (língua japonesa) a 文法 (gramática), formando 'a gramática do japonês'. は marca esse conjunto como tópico. 少し é um advérbio ('um pouco') que intensifica o adjetivo-い 難しい (difícil), que fecha a frase como predicado.
ops.issue: 少し é atenuador ('um pouco'); ele modera o grau de 難しい, não o intensifica. 'Intensifica' afirma o contrário da função do advérbio.

ops.current: このアパートは sets the subject ('as for this apartment')
ops.fix: このアパートは sets the topic ('as for this apartment')

The pair は...が here contrasts the general topic with the specific item.
ops.issue: After defining the structure as topic (は) + subject (が), the expl calls the は-phrase 'the subject', contradicting itself (ペットが is the subject) and the pt version, which correctly says 'define o assunto' (topic).

ops.issue: Wrong reading of 温く in context: beer losing its chill is ぬるい (lukewarm/tepid), read ぬるく. ぬくい 'nice and warm' is a regional/dialectal word and does not fit beer going warm; the gloss itself says 'lukewarm (losing its coolness)'.

ops.current: bi-ruganukukunatteshimatta
ops.fix: bi-ruganurukunatteshimatta
ops.issue: Same wrong reading carried into romaji: 温く should be romanized nuruku (from ぬるい 'lukewarm'), not nukuku.

ops.current: ぬくく
ops.fix: ぬるく
ops.issue: Token reading for 温く should be ぬるく (from ぬるい 'lukewarm', the standard word for drinks that lost their chill), not ぬくく (dialectal ぬくい 'nice and warm').

ops.current: As for the ashtray, it's already full.
ops.fix: The ashtray (が) is already full.
ops.issue: Literal mirror uses the topic device 'As for...' (the corpus's rendering of は) for the が-marked subject 灰皿が; the expl itself says が marks the subject, so the mirror conflates は and が for learners.

ops.current: Quanto ao cinzeiro, (ele) já (está) cheio.
ops.fix: O cinzeiro (が) já (está) cheio.
ops.issue: 'Quanto a...' is the corpus's は device, but 灰皿 is marked by が (subject). The literal mirror should show the subject relation, not a topic construction.

ops.current: As for the television, I put it on top of the stand.
ops.fix: The television, (I) put (it) on top of the stand.
ops.issue: Literal mirror renders the を-marked direct object (テレビを) with the topic device 'As for...', which this corpus reserves for は. It falsely shows the object as a topicalized element, misrepresenting the structure the lit field must mirror.

ops.current: Quanto à televisão, coloquei em cima do suporte.
ops.fix: A televisão (を), (eu) coloquei em cima do suporte.
ops.issue: 'Quanto a...' is the corpus's mirror of は, but here it renders the direct object marked by を (テレビを), hiding the object relation and implying a topic construction that is not in the Japanese.

ops.current: As for the bath, it has heated up, see.
ops.fix: The bath (が) has heated up, see.
ops.issue: Topic device 'As for...' applied to the が-marked subject お風呂が; the corpus reserves that device for は, and the expl correctly identifies が as subject marker, so the mirror contradicts the explanation.

ops.current: Quanto ao banho, ferveu, viu.
ops.fix: O banho (が) ferveu, viu.
ops.issue: 'Quanto a...' (は device) used for the が-marked subject お風呂が; the structural mirror should reflect the subject particle, matching the expl's own analysis.

ops.current: forma い (ren'yōkei) de 泊まる, ligada ao auxiliar de passado
ops.fix: forma de ligação de 泊まる com mudança de som (促音便: 泊まり→泊まっ), ligada ao auxiliar de passado た
ops.issue: Note mislabels 泊まっ as the ren'yōkei ('forma い') of 泊まる — the ren'yōkei is 泊まり; 泊まっ is the sokuonbin (sound-changed) stem used before た. The EN version of the note repeats the same error.

ops.current: As for the way, I (humbly) show/point it out.
ops.fix: The way, (I) humbly show/point (it) out.
ops.issue: Literal mirror renders the を-marked object (道を) with the topic device 'As for...', reserved for は in this corpus; it misrepresents 道 as a topic instead of the direct object of the humble verb.

ops.current: Quanto ao caminho, faço (humildemente) o ato de ensinar/indicar.
ops.fix: O caminho (を), faço (humildemente) o ato de ensinar/indicar.
ops.issue: 'Quanto a...' (the は device) is used for the を-marked direct object 道を, implying topicalization that does not exist in the Japanese; the structural mirror should keep 道 as object.

ops.current: marked by は, which establishes the sentence's subject
ops.fix: marked by は, which establishes the sentence's theme (what it is about)
ops.full_before: The topic is 今日 (きょう, today), marked by は, which establishes the sentence's subject. The actual subject is 宿題 (しゅくだい, homework), marked by が, and the verb of existence ある closes the sentence. The adverb たくさん (a lot, in large quantity) modifies the idea of how much exists. The target here is the vocabulary 宿題.
ops.issue: Wording says は 'establishes the sentence's subject', then the next sentence says 'the actual subject is 宿題' — self-contradictory use of 'subject' for the topic. The pt version correctly uses 'assunto' (theme).

ops.current: くすりをのんだきごうするとあたまがいたくなくなった
ops.fix: くすりをのんだするとあたまがいたくなくなった
ops.issue: The full-width space in the JP was transcribed as きごう ('symbol' = 記号), inserting a phantom word into the phonetic reading: '...のんだ きごう すると...'. Reading it aloud produces a non-existent word.

ops.current: kusurionondakigousurutoatamagaitakunakunatta
ops.fix: kusurionondasurutoatamagaitakunakunatta
ops.issue: Same space-as-きごう bug leaked into romaji as 'kigou' (a phantom word). This is not the recorded punctuation/katakana known issue — it is an inserted wrong reading.

ops.current: O foco de vocabulário (alvo 1286) é o verbo 訪ねる.
ops.fix: O foco de vocabulário é o verbo 訪ねる.
ops.full_before: 日曜日に traz a partícula に marcando o ponto no tempo (no domingo). O objeto direto 祖父母 (avós) é marcado por を, e o verbo 訪ねる (visitar) aparece em 訪ねた, sua forma passada simples (informal). O foco de vocabulário (alvo 1286) é o verbo 訪ねる.
ops.issue: Internal pipeline artifact '(alvo 1286)' (a target-item ID) leaked into the learner-facing pt explanation; expl_en has no such reference, so the two versions also diverge.

ops.current: のーとをいちさつずつかった
ops.fix: のーとをいっさつずつかった
ops.issue: 一冊 is read いっさつ (issatsu, with gemination before さ), not いちさつ. The kana teaches a wrong reading of the counter word.

ops.current: いち
ops.fix: いっ
ops.issue: Token 一 in the compound 一冊 has reading いち; in context it geminates to いっ (一冊 = いっさつ), matching the pattern 一冊/一回/一杯.

ops.current: no-tooichisatsuzutsukatta
ops.fix: no-tooissatsuzutsukatta
ops.issue: Romaji carries the same wrong reading 'ichisatsu' for 一冊; correct is 'issatsu' (geminated).

ops.current: past form of 頼む (stem 頼ん + 〜だ, with i-onbin voicing)
ops.fix: en: "past form of 頼む (stem 頼ん + 〜だ, with nasal onbin 撥音便 む→ん; た voices to だ)"; pt-BR: "forma passada de 頼む (raiz 頼ん + 〜だ, com onbin nasal 撥音便 む→ん; た sonoriza para だ)"
ops.issue: Conjugation note (both en and pt-BR) says 頼んだ shows 'i-onbin voicing' (い音便). Wrong: 頼む→頼んだ is 撥音便 (hatsuonbin, nasal onbin, む→ん); い音便 is the 書いた/泳いだ type. Teaches a false conjugation classification.

ops.current: あさきごうろくじにきごうおきる
ops.fix: あさろくじにおきる
ops.issue: Both spaces in the JP were transcribed as きごう ('symbol'), inserting the phantom word twice into the phonetic reading: あさ きごう ろくじに きごう おきる.

ops.current: asakigourokujinikigouokiru
ops.fix: asarokujiniokiru
ops.issue: Same bug in romaji: 'kigou' inserted twice for the spaces. Not the recorded punctuation/katakana known issue — it is an inserted wrong reading.

ops.current: already
ops.fix: no more, (not) anymore
ops.issue: In もうない, もう + negative means '(not) anymore / no more', not 'already' (its affirmative sense). The en gloss fits the other sense; the pt gloss 'já' works because pt-BR uses 'já não'.

ops.current: That cup is made of glass.
ops.fix: This cup is made of glass.
ops.issue: この means 'this' (proximal), but the natural EN translation uses the distal 'That cup'. Demonstrative mismatch with the JP; lit_en itself correctly uses 'this'. In a course teaching ko-so-a-do this misteaches the contrast.

ops.current: this/that
ops.fix: this
ops.issue: この is glossed 'this/that'; この is proximal only — 'that' belongs to その/あの. Other sentences in the corpus gloss この correctly as 'this'.

ops.current: caro (forma て: 'mesmo que seja caro')
ops.fix: caro
ops.issue: The pt gloss claims 高い is a て-form meaning 'mesmo que seja caro' (even if expensive) — a copy-paste leftover from a 〜ても sentence. Here 高い is the plain dictionary-form predicate, exactly as the token's own note says. Teaches a false conjugation.

ops.current: As for the room, after making it clean, I put away the books.
ops.fix: Making the room clean, and after that, I put away the books.
ops.issue: 部屋を is the を-marked direct object of きれいにする, not a topic. 'As for the room' is the mirror reserved for は-topics and misrepresents the structure (there is no は in the sentence).

ops.current: Quanto ao quarto, tornando-o bonito/limpo, e a partir daí, guardei os livros.
ops.fix: Tornando o quarto limpo/bonito, e a partir daí, guardei os livros.
ops.issue: Mesma falha estrutural: 'Quanto ao quarto' apresenta o objeto marcado por を como se fosse tópico marcado por は; o espelho literal deve refletir 部屋を como objeto de きれいにする.

ops.current: むずかしいことばがありますきごうたとえばこのかんじ
ops.fix: むずかしいことばがあります たとえばこのかんじ
ops.issue: Extra syllables きごう ('symbol') injected between あります and たとえば — the whitespace token's bogus reading (tokens[5]) leaked into the transcription. The word きごう does not exist in the sentence.

ops.current: muzukashiikotobagaarimasukigoutatoebakonokanji
ops.fix: muzukashiikotobagaarimasutatoebakonokanji
ops.issue: Same leak as kana: spurious 'kigou' inserted mid-sentence; not part of the Japanese.

ops.current: ねこがのきのもとでねている
ops.fix: ねこがのきのしたでねている
ops.issue: 軒の下 (physically under the eaves) is read のきのした (cf. 軒下 のきした); もと is the reading of 下 only in abstract expressions like 法の下・空の下. Wrong reading in context.

ops.current: nekoganokinomotodeneteiru
ops.fix: nekoganokinoshitadeneteiru
ops.issue: Mirrors the kana error: 'motode' should be 'shitade' (軒の下 = noki no shita).

ops.current: もと
ops.fix: した
ops.issue: Reading of 下 in 軒の下 is した (physical 'underneath', matching the token's own gloss 'parte de baixo, embaixo'); もと applies only to abstract 下 (法の下, 旗の下).

ops.current: As for the cat, it's sleeping under the eaves.
ops.fix: The cat, under the eaves, is sleeping.
ops.issue: 猫が is a が-marked subject (the expl itself stresses が presents new information), but the literal uses the topic device 'As for the cat', which mirrors は. Contradicts the sentence's own explanation and blurs は vs が.

ops.current: Quanto ao gato, embaixo do beiral está dormindo.
ops.fix: O gato, embaixo do beiral, está dormindo.
ops.issue: Mesma falha: 'Quanto ao gato' aplica o espelho de tópico (は) a um sujeito marcado por が, contradizendo a própria expl_pt, que destaca が como sujeito/informação nova.

ops.current: He bought three apples.
ops.fix: (I) bought three apples.
ops.issue: lit_en uses subject 'He' while en uses 'I'. The JP is subjectless; default reading (and the en/pt/expl) is first person. Contradictory subject in the literal mirror confuses learners.

ops.current: forma 買っ (passado) de 買う, com sonorização antes de た
ops.fix: forma 買っ (passado) de 買う, com geminação (促音便, っ) antes de た
ops.issue: pt-BR note says 買った involves 'sonorização' (voicing) before た. False: 買う→買った is 促音便 (gemination, っ); no voicing occurs (voicing would give だ, as in 読んだ). Teaches a wrong conjugation fact; the en note ('sound change') is vague but not wrong.

ops.current: In free time, as for movies, I watch them.
ops.fix: In free time, movies (object), I watch.
ops.issue: 'as for movies' renders the を-marked direct object 映画を as a topic construction; there is no は on 映画. Contradicts the expl, which correctly calls 映画 the direct object marked by を.

ops.current: Em época que é livre, quanto a filme, assisto.
ops.fix: Em época que é livre, filme (objeto), assisto.
ops.issue: 'quanto a filme' applies the は-topic mirror device to 映画を, which is a を-marked direct object, not a topic. Misteaches particle function and contradicts the expl (objeto direto marcado por を).

ops.current: O verbo 走ります (andar/correr) está na forma polite (ます).
ops.fix: O verbo 走ります (andar/correr) está na forma polida (ます).
ops.full_before: A estrutura é tópico (車は = quanto ao carro) seguido do que ele faz. O verbo 走ります (andar/correr) está na forma polite (ます). Aqui 左側を (o lado esquerdo) usa を porque é o trajeto/espaço percorrido pelo movimento, um uso especial de を com verbos de deslocamento.
ops.issue: English word 'polite' left untranslated in the pt-BR explanation; the corpus elsewhere consistently uses 'polida/polido' (cf. same item's token note 'forma polida').

ops.current: As for every month, on the 1st, I do the cleaning.
ops.fix: Every month, on the 1st, I do the cleaning.
ops.issue: 'As for every month' fabricates a topic construction; 毎月１日 is a single time expression marked only by に (no は). The 'as for' device should be reserved for は.

ops.current: Quanto a todo mês, no dia 1, faço a limpeza.
ops.fix: Todo mês, no dia 1, faço a limpeza.
ops.issue: 'Quanto a todo mês' applies the は-topic mirror device to 毎月, which carries no は; 毎月１日 is one time expression with に. Misleads learners scanning for a topic particle.

ops.current: economy
ops.fix: economics
ops.issue: 経済 glossed as 'economy', but in 大学で経済を勉強しています it is the academic discipline, i.e. 'economics' (as the en translation itself says). Gloss fits another sense of the word, not this context.

ops.current: funciona sozinho como predicado, sем precisar de です
ops.fix: funciona sozinho como predicado, sem precisar de です
ops.full_before: Frase do tipo 'A é adjetivo'. O tópico この神社 (este santuário) é marcado por は, とても é o advérbio de intensidade ('muito'), e 古い é um い-adjetivo que funciona sozinho como predicado, sем precisar de です no registro casual. O alvo de vocabulário aqui é 神社 (santuário).
ops.issue: Encoding defect: the word 'sem' is written with Cyrillic letters е (U+0435) and м (U+043C) — 'sем' — instead of Latin characters.

ops.current: dia(do mês) (sufixo contador)
